words.sense: Impartial because one has no personal stake in the outcome.
misconceptions: Assuming an attentive judge cannot be impartial.
Confusing indifference to an activity with fairness in judging outcomes.

words.sense: Not curious, engaged, or eager to take part.
misconceptions: Mistaking lack of personal stake for lack of curiosity.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Amal’s role as a poster judge?

beats.text: Amal knew none of the entrants and would gain nothing from any result, so she scored every poster by the same criteria.
beats.decisive_clue: no personal stake and equal judging criteria
beats.reason: No personal stake and equal judging criteria. Impartial because one has no personal stake in the outcome.

beats.text: She spent hours examining the smallest details.
beats.decisive_clue: careful attention does not create a conflict of interest
beats.reason: Careful attention does not create a conflict of interest. Impartial because one has no personal stake in the outcome.

chains.feedback_short: Careful attention does not create a conflict of interest.
chains.feedback_deep: Disinterested means impartial because one has no personal stake in the outcome; uninterested means not curious, engaged, or eager to take part. Here, no personal stake and equal judging criteria. The new detail does not change the deciding fact: careful attention does not create a conflict of interest. Thus disinterested remains the stronger choice.
chains.contrast_rule: Disinterested can judge fairly; uninterested does not care to engage.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Jae’s attitude toward the exhibition?

beats.text: Jae declined a free ticket to the exhibition because he had no desire to see the paintings.
beats.decisive_clue: he has no desire to experience the exhibition
beats.reason: He has no desire to experience the exhibition. Uninterested means not curious, engaged, or eager to take part.

beats.text: Even an offer of a private guided tour failed to make him curious about the art.
beats.decisive_clue: he still lacks curiosity despite the more appealing invitation
beats.reason: He still lacks curiosity despite the more appealing invitation. That describes unwillingness to engage, not impartiality.

chains.feedback_short: A better invitation still does not create curiosity.
chains.feedback_deep: Disinterested means impartial because one has no personal stake in an outcome; uninterested means not curious, engaged, or eager to take part. Jae repeatedly shows no desire to engage with the exhibition. The improved invitation does not change that lack of curiosity, so uninterested remains the stronger choice.
chains.contrast_rule: Disinterested describes impartiality; uninterested describes a lack of curiosity or engagement.
